chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:

Al-Rida عليه السلام sent a gift to my father, so my father wrote to him: ‘Is khums due upon me concerning what you sent to me?’ He wrote to him: ‘There is no khums upon you regarding what the owner of the khums sends.’

key_terms.بِصِلَةٍ: a gift or financial present sent to someone
key_terms.خُمُسٌ: the one-fifth due on certain categories of wealth
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْخُمُسِ: the one vested with rightful authority over khums
key_terms.لَا خُمُسَ عَلَيْكَ: no khums is obligatory upon you

ai.seo_question: Is khums due on a gift sent by the Imam عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that when Imam al-Rida عليه السلام sent a gift, no khums was due upon the recipient for that specific transfer. It indicates a legal ruling concerning wealth received from the one who possesses authority over khums.
